narrative:
On September 19, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 42.8%, taking up 805 of the 1,879 scheduled cases across 40 judges. This reflects consistent performance relative to recent days, closely matching the 42.0% clearance recorded on September 18 (1,182 of 2,812 heard) and 41.5% on September 17, despite a lower overall volume of scheduled matters.

Bench-level output revealed stark contrasts in docket management. Strong throughput among high-volume rosters was driven by Justice K. Manmadha Rao, who heard 60 of 82 cases (73.2%), Justice E.S. Indiresh, clearing 53 of 64 listings (82.8%), and Justice H.P. Sandesh, disposing of 49 of 67 matters (73.1%). Conversely, significant cause-list stagnation was observed in Hall 7, where Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard just 1 of 279 matters on an expansive list (0.4%). Benches under Justice Suraj Govindaraj (101 scheduled across multiple rosters) and Justice C.M. Poonacha (55 scheduled) conducted no hearings.

Stage-wise conversion showed significant efficiency in procedural categories. Matters listed for Orders reached a 65.9% hearing rate (299 of 454 heard), representing a sharp gain over the 47.8% conversion rate logged on September 18. Preliminary Hearings also advanced steadily at 65.1% (121 of 186). However, Further Hearing stages stalled almost entirely, converting just 2.5% of cases (8 of 322), while Admission hearings dropped to 40.1% from 51.3% on the previous day. 

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket with 773 scheduled cases and converted at 33.6%, remaining largely consistent with the 32.1% recorded on September 18. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) demonstrated stronger clearance at 54.2% and 71.4% respectively, while Regular First Appeals (RFA) and Regular Second Appeals (RSA) saw limited progress at 24.0% and 25.0%.
